# What steps 3–6 actually found — and one conclusion of ours that they overturn

**Written 2026-09-12, autonomously, from `STEPS_3_TO_6.md`.** That file is generated by
`mine_steps3to6.py` and must not be hand-edited; this one is the reading of it. Every
number below is in the generated tables and can be re-derived by re-running the script.

**Status: not yet quotable in the manuscript.** The instrument is still uncalibrated —
one of the two predicate thresholds is inherited rather than derived, and that is the
measurement pass, which has not run. What follows is robust to everything *else* the
order of work asked for.

---

## 1. The headline survives every step asked of it

The partner effect was previously reported per backbone on **row-level rates with no
interval**. It now survives all four of the corrections `FIRST_LOOK.md` demanded:

| correction | effect on the headline |
|---|---|
| unit → **paralog cluster**, not row | survives |
| **cluster bootstrap** intervals | **all 12 role × backbone contrasts exclude zero** |
| readout → **continuous** `pocket_ca_rmsd` | survives |
| **seeds** collapsed inside receptor | survives |
| **opsins** handled explicitly, both ways | survives under both |

Binary predicate, apo → cognate, cluster unit, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI:

| backbone | agonist | antagonist | decoy |
|---|---|---|---|
| protenix | **+0.922** [+0.863, +0.977] | +0.978 | +0.959 |
| boltz | **+0.785** [+0.628, +0.911] | +0.802 | +0.759 |
| of3 | **+0.599** [+0.472, +0.715] | +0.654 | +0.604 |
| chai | **+0.343** [+0.161, +0.537] | +0.318 | +0.395 |

**The backbones differ by a factor of about three** — chai ≈ +0.34, protenix ≈ +0.92 —
which is why nothing here is pooled and why no pooled number should ever be quoted.
The *sign and significance* are unanimous; the *magnitude* is not.

## 2. THE CORRECTION — "decoy ≈ antagonist" was an artefact of the binary predicate

**This is the most important thing in the file, and it overturns a reading we have been
carrying since the data landed.**

We reported that the decoy and the neutral antagonist were indistinguishable on all four
backbones (+0.011, −0.004, −0.016, −0.004), and treated that as a finding about the
decoy set — evidence that the frozen campaign's decoys were never a controlled negative.

**Both halves need restating.**

**(a) That comparison was of the apo→cognate SHIFT, and the shift genuinely is
ligand-independent.** All three ligand classes move by the same amount when the partner
arrives. That part stands, and it is a real result: **the partner effect does not depend
on what is in the pocket.**

**(b) But the LEVEL is not ligand-independent, and the binary predicate could not see
it.** On the continuous readout the three classes separate significantly, in a
consistent order, on essentially every backbone and in both arms:

> **agonist > decoy > antagonist**, nearest-active first.

At apo/boltz, mean Δ(inactive − active), positive = nearer active:
agonist **−0.120**, decoy **−0.289**, antagonist **−0.401**.
`antagonist − decoy` excludes zero on **7 of 8** (arm × backbone) cells on the
continuous readout, and on **2 of 8** on the binary one.

**Why the binary predicate missed it:** it is floor-pinned in apo — rates of 0.01–0.35 —
so a real shift in pocket geometry that does not cross both thresholds scores as no
change at all. `SC-C-6` said this would happen and said to prefer the continuous
readout. **This is that warning coming true, measured.**

**The ordering is biologically coherent**, which is part of why it is believable: a
neutral antagonist actively stabilises the inactive state; a decoy does nothing, so the
receptor sits at its unliganded preference; the agonist pushes toward active. A decoy
falling *between* the two is what that predicts.

**Consequence for `DECISIONS.md` F-19.** F-19 argues the frozen decoy arm was not a
controlled negative, and it still stands on its own evidence — the decoys fail their
own property window on 3–5 of 6 axes and are systematically mischarged. **But
"decoy ≈ antagonist" may no longer be cited in support of it.** On the readout the drop
itself prefers, the decoy is *not* the antagonist. F-19's argument must rest on the
chemistry, which is where its evidence actually is.

---

## 3. C7 is answered — and the two readouts disagree about how big it is

Title clause C7 is *"the agonist alone does not drive the active state."*

**On the binary predicate, C7 holds comfortably.** Agonist-alone in apo runs
0.011–0.324 across backbones, against cognate 0.637–0.989. Agonist minus antagonist
*within* apo is **+0.044 to +0.066**, significant on 3 of 4 backbones — a real but small
lift, against a partner effect of **+0.78**. So the ligand contributes of order **8%** of
what the partner does.

**On the continuous readout the ligand does considerably more than that.**
Agonist − antagonist in apo is **+0.13 to +0.28**, significant on **4 of 4**, against a
partner effect of about **+0.62**. That is of order **30–45%**.

**Both cannot be quoted.** They are the same comparison read through two instruments,
one of which is pinned against a floor. The continuous readout is the one `SC-C-6`
tells us to prefer and the one that is not pinned — so the honest statement is:

> The agonist alone does not reproduce the partner's effect on any backbone, but it is
> not inert: on the continuous pocket readout it accounts for roughly a third of the
> partner's shift, with intervals excluding zero on all four backbones.

That is a **weaker** version of C7 than the binary table suggests and a **stronger**
statement about ligands than this project has been making. It should be written that
way, and it bears directly on `vo2026fiducials` p.8, where a high-efficacy agonist alone
drove β2AR TM6 *"almost complete outward movement"* — our result is no longer flatly
inconsistent with theirs.

## 3b. The result was tested against its most obvious confound and survived

**The G4 off-site gate is the reason this section exists.** In the apo arm the
off-site rate (`distance_A > 15 Å`, the gate's own threshold) is severely
**role-asymmetric**:

| apo role | n | off-site |
|---|---:|---:|
| full_agonist | 7,000 | **29.30%** |
| neutral_antagonist | 5,800 | **1.62%** |
| decoy_lig | 7,200 | **12.25%** |

So §3's contrast compares a population where roughly **a third of the agonist rows have
no agonist in the pocket** against one where almost every antagonist row does. If C7 were
an empty-pocket artefact — the receptor drifting active because nothing is bound — then
restricting to on-site rows should collapse it.

**It does not.** Agonist − antagonist in apo, continuous readout, cluster unit:

| backbone | all rows | on-site only |
|---|---|---|
| boltz | +0.281 [+0.146, +0.413] | **+0.303** [+0.175, +0.450] |
| chai | +0.132 [+0.053, +0.209] | **+0.110** [+0.042, +0.180] |
| of3 | +0.253 [+0.108, +0.412] | **+0.237** [+0.057, +0.443] |
| protenix | +0.189 [+0.093, +0.292] | **+0.149** [+0.090, +0.200] |

All four still exclude zero; the magnitudes barely move and in no systematic direction.
The restriction costs clusters (14 → 10–11) because receptors that are 100% off-site
leave entirely, which is why the intervals widen.

**The join that makes this possible is exact and was verified, not assumed:** all 40,000
rows of `g4_full_census_v2.csv` match a `rows.tier3.v2.csv` row on `input_path`, and the
800 unmatched tier3 rows are precisely the opsins, which the census does not cover. The
script **fails** rather than proceeding if that match is not exactly 40,000.

**What this does and does not close.** It closes the question *"is the ligand effect an
empty-pocket artefact?"* — no. It does **not** discharge the G4 gate itself, which is
about `SC-C-1`'s quoted 1.52% off-site being computed on a different population from the
one SC-C-1 runs on (18.92% on the 23 common receptors; 35.85% on its agonist half). That
remains `ASKS.md` B3.

## 4. What switching readout costs, measured

The continuous readout is **all-or-nothing per receptor**: 28 complete, **10 absent, 0
partial**, and absent symmetrically across both arms and all three roles.

- clusters: **22 → 18**; MDE `1.218/√k`: **0.260 → 0.287**, a 10.4% loss of sensitivity.
- **no role or arm bias is introduced** — the question that mattered, since a readout
  missing asymmetrically across roles would have biased every ligand-class comparison
  the way the opsin exclusion does.

Lost entirely: ACM1, ADA2A, ADRB1, B1B1U5, CCKAR, DRD3, EDNRA, HRH3, OPSD, OX2R.

---

## 5. Two data defects worth reporting upstream

1. **`A_RECEPTOR_SLUG_MISSING` never fires.** The 800 opsin rows carry an empty
   `receptor_slug` *and* an empty `receptor_class`, and the flag that exists to mark
   exactly that condition is **empty on all 800**. A flag that vouches for the data and
   does not fire is Block A's `matches_claim_sheet` defect in another costume. The
   identity is recoverable from `input_path` — `b1b1u5` and `opsd`, 400 each — so
   nothing is lost, but nothing in the file says so.
2. **Every opsin row is `full_agonist`.** Dropping them for an empty class, as the
   first-look table did, removes agonist observations only. Both variants are now
   reported and the headline is unchanged under either, but any future table that drops
   them silently is comparing levels on populations they do not share.

---

## 6. Seeds

712 design cells, 5 seeds each. **524 (73.6%) are unanimous across seeds.** Mean
seed-to-seed spread within a cell is 0.083. Seeds are collapsed inside the receptor
before the cluster mean everywhere in `STEPS_3_TO_6.md`, so five seeds of one receptor
cannot outvote one seed of another.

---

## 7. What is still not settled

- **The instrument is uncalibrated.** One predicate threshold is inherited. Everything
  above is conditional on it. → the measurement pass.
- **Modality is confounded with receptor identity.** Every peptide-ligand row is a
  peptide-family receptor. → the T3 within-receptor contrast, `D-2026-09-12-f`.
- **The G4 off-site gate fired on 8 of 12 cells and its remedy was never applied.** This
  file was supposed to unblock it; that has not been done here.
